What triggers what

Softprepositions am, ar, at, dan, dros, drwy, heb, hyd, gan, wrth, i, o · y + feminine singular · adjective after feminine singular · yn + adjective / noun · dau, dwy · un + feminine · dy, ei (his) · object of an inflected verb · i + person + verbnoun (cyn i fi fynd) · past-tense questions and negatives

ll and rh resist soft mutation after y (feminine), un (feminine) and yn: y llwy, un llaw, yn llawn.

units.title: Bod: present
units.subtitle: Dw i, mae e, maen nhw
units.rule:
Present = bod + yn ('n) + verbnoun. Dw i'n dysgu. I learn / I'm learning. Use 'n after a vowel, yn after a consonant: Mae Siân yn dysgu.

StatementQuestion
IDw iYdw i?
youRwyt ti / Ti'nWyt ti?
he / sheMae e / Mae hiYdy e? / Ydy hi?
nounMae Siân / Mae'r plantYdy Siân? / Ydy'r plant?
weDyn niYdyn ni?
you (pl / polite)Dych chiYdych chi? / Dych chi?
theyMaen nhwYdyn nhw?

Rule: a noun subject always takes mae / ydy, even if plural. Mae'r plant yn chwarae. Maen and ydyn only go with nhw (and ni).

Yes / no: no single word. Answer with the verb, for the person answering: Wyt ti...? → Ydw / Nac ydw. Ydy e...? → Ydy / Nac ydy. Ydyn nhw...? → Ydyn / Nac ydyn.

questions.explain: First person statement: Dw i. Ydw i is the question form; Dydw i needs ddim.
Statement with nhw: Maen nhw. Ydyn nhw is the question.
A noun subject always takes mae, even a plural one. Maen only goes with nhw.
Answer with the verb of the question: Ydy hi? → Ydy.
The answer is about me, so use the 'I' answer form: Ydw. Do is only for past-tense questions.

questions.prompt: Dych chi'n siarad Cymraeg? (No, I don't)
questions.explain: No = Nac + the verb for the person answering: Nac ydw. Naddo is only for past-tense questions.
Dyn ni + 'n + verbnoun.
Question form for he: Ydy e?
Maen nhw. Also: i causes soft mutation, Caerdydd → Gaerdydd.
Noun subject takes mae, not maen. (Mae + y contracts to mae'r.)
The question form for ti is Wyt ti?
Question form for nhw: Ydyn nhw?
Answering about them: Ydyn (they are).
Noun subject: Ydy. After a consonant use the full yn; 'n only follows a vowel.
Plant ends in a consonant, so the full yn.

units.termDef: A tense places an action in time. The present covers what is happening now and what is generally true. Welsh builds it from bod + yn + verbnoun, so Dw i'n mynd means both 'I am going' (present continuous) and 'I go' (simple present). A verbnoun is the dictionary form of a verb, like 'going / to go'.

units.title: Negatives: present
units.subtitle: Dw i ddim, does dim
units.rule:
Negative = verb + subject + ddim + yn + verbnoun. No 'n straight after the subject. Dw i ddim yn gwybod.

Negative
IDw i ddim
youDwyt ti ddim
he / sheDyw e ddim / Dyw hi ddim
(North: Dydy e ddim)
definite nounDyw'r bws ddim / Dyw Tom ddim
weDyn ni ddim
you (pl)Dych chi ddim
theyDyn nhw ddim / Dydyn nhw ddim

There is / isn't: Mae llaeth (there's milk) → Does dim llaeth (there's no milk). Does dim is only for an indefinite noun. With a definite one use dyw: Dyw'r llaeth ddim yma.

options: Dw i ddim yn gweithio heddiw.
Dw i dim yn gweithio heddiw.
Dw i'n ddim yn gweithio heddiw.
Dw i ddim yn weithio heddiw.
Dydw i dim yn gweithio heddiw.
questions.explain: Subject + ddim + yn + verbnoun. Ddim (mutated dim), no 'n on the subject, and keep the yn.
Dyw e ddim + yn + verbnoun. (Dydy e ddim is also correct.)
Definite noun subject (y bws): dyw. Does dim is only for indefinite nouns.
Indefinite 'there isn't': Does dim + noun. Dim stays unmutated, and so does the noun.

questions.sentence: Dw i dim yn hoffi te.
questions.fix: Dw i ddim yn hoffi te.
questions.explain: After the subject it is ddim (mutated), not dim.

questions.answer: Dyn ni ddim yn byw yma
questions.explain: Dyn ni ddim yn...
Negative marker after the subject: ddim.
Negative of maen nhw is dyn / dydyn nhw ddim. Maen never takes ddim.
Does only goes with indefinite nouns (does dim plant = there are no children). For 'the children', use dyw.
Dyw = present. Hi is used for weather 'it'. Oer = cold (old = hen).

questions.en: There's no bread in the house.
questions.explain: Indefinite noun (bara): Does dim.

questions.prompt: Make negative: Mae Tom yn y gwaith.
options: Dyw Tom ddim yn y gwaith.
Does Tom ddim yn y gwaith.
Dyw Tom dim yn y gwaith.
Dyn Tom ddim yn y gwaith.
Does dim Tom yn y gwaith.
Dyw Tom ddim yn y waith.
questions.explain: A name is definite: Dyw Tom ddim.

questions.prompt: Make negative: Mae plant yn yr ardd.
options: Does dim plant yn yr ardd.
Dyw plant ddim yn yr ardd.
Does plant ddim yn yr ardd.
Dyw dim plant yn yr ardd.
Does ddim plant yn yr ardd.
Dyw'r plant ddim yn yr ardd.
questions.explain: Indefinite subject (plant, no 'the'): Does dim + noun.

units.termDef: Negation turns a positive statement into a 'not' statement. In Welsh the verb changes shape (dw → dw i ddim, mae → dyw … ddim) and ddim or dim is added.

units.title: Soft mutation
units.subtitle: i Gaerdydd, y gath, cath fawr
units.rule:
Soft mutation (treiglad meddal) changes the first letter:

p → bt → dc → g
b → fd → ddg → (drops)
m → fll → lrh → r

Main triggers

  • Prepositions: am, ar, at, dan, dros, drwy, heb, hyd, gan, wrth, i, o. i Gaerdydd, o Fangor, heb laeth
  • y / 'r + feminine singular noun: y gath (but y ci, masculine)
  • Adjective after a feminine singular noun: cath fawr (but ci mawr)
  • dau / dwy: dau gi, dwy gath
  • yn + adjective or noun (description): Mae hi'n dal. Mae e'n feddyg. Not yn + verbnoun: yn canu.
  • Object of an inflected verb: Prynais i gar.

Exception: ll and rh do not change after y (feminine) or yn: y llwy, yn llawn. They do change after prepositions: heb laeth.

questions.explain: i causes soft mutation: c → g.
o causes soft mutation: b → f.
y + feminine singular noun: soft mutation.
Adjective after a feminine singular noun: m → f.
Ci is masculine: no mutation of the adjective.
dau / dwy + soft mutation, and the noun stays singular.
yn + adjective: soft mutation, t → d.
yn + noun (describing): soft mutation, m → f.
Exception: ll does not mutate after yn.
Exception: ll does not mutate after y, even with a feminine noun.
After a preposition, ll does mutate: llaeth → laeth.
Object straight after an inflected verb + subject: soft mutation.
Merch is feminine (mutates after y); bachgen is masculine (does not). And + the = a'r.
i causes soft mutation.
Dyn is masculine: no mutation after y / 'r.
Soft mutation b → f. Ym Mangor means in Bangor (nasal mutation after yn).
Tŷ is masculine: no mutation of the adjective.

questions.en: She went from Bangor to Cardiff.
questions.answer: Aeth hi o Fangor i Gaerdydd
questions.explain: o and i both trigger soft mutation.
yn + adjective: g drops. Gwlyb → wlyb.

units.termDef: A mutation is a regular change to the first consonant of a word, caused by the word before it (the trigger). Soft mutation is the most common: p→b, t→d, c→g, b→f, d→dd, g drops, m→f, ll→l, rh→r.

units.title: My, your, his, her
units.subtitle: fy nghar, ei char hi
units.rule:
Possessives go before the noun and trigger a mutation. The pronoun after is common but optional.

WordMutationcarenw
fy (my)nasalfy nghar ify enw i
dy (your)softdy gar didy enw di
ei (his)softei gar eei enw e
ei (her)aspirate + hei char hiei henw hi
ein (our)h before vowelein car niein henw ni
eich (your pl)noneeich car chieich enw chi
eu (their)h before voweleu car nhweu henw nhw

Nasal: c → ngh, p → mh, t → nh, g → ng, b → m, d → n.
Aspirate: c → ch, p → ph, t → th (others unchanged).

Ei his / her look identical; the mutation (and e / hi) tells you which.

questions.explain: fy + nasal: t → nh.
fy + nasal: b → m.
fy + nasal: g → ng.
ei (her) + aspirate: c → ch.
ei (his) + soft: c → g.
dy + soft: m → f.
ei (her) adds h before a vowel.
ein adds h before a vowel (y counts as a vowel).
eich causes no mutation.
ei (her) + aspirate: t → th.
eu only adds h before vowels; ff never mutates.
His: soft mutation, which doesn't affect vowels. Her adds h: ei henw hi.
m is unaffected by the nasal mutation: fy mam.

questions.sentence: Mae fy car i yn y garej.
questions.fix: Mae fy nghar i yn y garej.
questions.explain: fy + nasal mutation: car → nghar.
fy + nasal: t → nh.
Her: aspirate, c → ch. Ei gar would mean his car.
eu causes no consonant mutation; it only adds h before vowels.

questions.answer: Mae ei frawd e'n gweithio heddiw
questions.explain: ei (his) + soft: b → f.

units.termDef: Possessive determiners say whose something is: my, your, his, her, our, their. In Welsh they come before the noun, often trigger a mutation, and are echoed by a pronoun after it: fy nghar i (my car).

units.title: Past tense
units.subtitle: Prynais i, es i, ces i
units.rule:
Regular: stem + ending. Stem = verbnoun minus its ending (prynu → pryn-, codi → cod-, bwyta → bwyt-, yfed → yf-). Some stems are irregular: gweld → gwel-, aros → arhos-, gadael → gadaw-, cerdded → cerdd-.

Prynais iPrynon ni
Prynaist tiPrynoch chi
Prynodd e / hiPrynon nhw

Irregular four:

mynddodcaelgwneud
Es iDes iCes iGwnes i
Est tiDest tiCest tiGwnest ti
Aeth eDaeth eCafodd eGwnaeth e
Aethon niDaethon niCawson niGwnaethon ni

Question: soft-mutate the verb. Brynaist ti? Gest ti? Answer Do / Naddo for any person.

Negative: mutate + ddim. Brynais i ddim. Formally c, p, t take the aspirate: Ches i ddim, Phrynais i ddim.

The object soft-mutates: Prynais i gar.

questions.explain: Mynd is irregular: Es i.
Every past-tense question is answered Do / Naddo.
He / she ending: -odd.
We ending: -on. Bwyta → bwyt- → bwyton ni.

options: Dw i ddim yn prynu dim byd.
questions.explain: Negative: mutate the verb + ddim. Formal written form: Phrynais i ddim byd.
Past-tense questions soft-mutate the verb: g drops.

questions.en: Did you have a good time?
questions.explain: Cest ti → question soft-mutates: Gest ti?
Past-tense no: Naddo.
Dod is irregular: Daethon nhw.
Gwneud: Gwnes i. Fy + nasal: gwaith → ngwaith.
I ending: -ais. -on is we / they.
Darllen → darllen- + ais.
Negative of ces i: Ches i ddim (Ges i ddim is also heard).
Mynd, he / she: Aeth.
Dod, they: daethon. Question soft-mutates: Ddaethon nhw?
Tal- + och = Taloch. Question soft-mutates: Daloch chi?

units.termDef: The simple past (preterite) describes a completed action at a point in the past: 'I went', 'she bought'. Welsh adds personal endings to the verb stem: an inflected or short-form verb (prynais i, prynodd hi).

units.title: Cyn i, ar ôl i, rhaid i
units.subtitle: cyn i fi golli'r bws
units.rule:
Equation: cyn / ar ôl / wrth / nes / er mwyn + i + person + soft-mutated verbnoun.

cyn i fi golli'r bws = before I miss the bus.

i fii ni
i tii chi
iddo fe / iddi hiiddyn nhw
with a noun: i'r bws, i Siân

No tense of its own. The main clause sets the time: Gadawais i cyn iddo fe gyrraedd (before he arrived). Bydda i'n gadael cyn iddo fe gyrraedd (before he arrives).

cyn ibefore
ar ôl iafter
wrth ias / while
nes iuntil
er mwyn iso that

Rhaid i (must) works the same: Rhaid i fi fynd.

Shortcuts: same subject in both halves → drop i + person: Bwytais i cyn mynd. Before a plain noun → no i: cyn y cyfarfod, ar ôl cinio.

questions.en: I must go before I miss the bus.
questions.answer: Rhaid i fi fynd cyn i fi golli'r bws
questions.explain: Rhaid i fi + soft (fynd); cyn i fi + soft (golli).
i + person + soft mutation: m → f.
i inflects for he: iddo fe. Then soft mutation: cyrraedd → gyrraedd.
i + person + soft mutation: c → g.
Before a plain noun (no verb), no i: cyn y cyfarfod.

questions.answer: Gadawais i cyn iddi hi gyrraedd
questions.explain: Iddi hi + soft mutation. The past meaning comes from Gadawais.

questions.sentence: Ar ôl i ni bwyta, aethon ni allan.
questions.fix: Ar ôl i ni fwyta, aethon ni allan.
questions.explain: The verbnoun after i + person soft-mutates: bwyta → fwyta.

questions.sentence: Cyn dw i'n mynd adre, rhaid i fi siopa.
questions.fix: Cyn i fi fynd adre, rhaid i fi siopa.
questions.explain: No normal tense after cyn. Use i + person + mutated verbnoun.

questions.prompt: Wrth i fi gerdded adre, dechreuodd hi fwrw glaw.
options: As I was walking home, it started to rain.
Before I walked home, it started to rain.
After I walked home, it started to rain.
Until I walked home, it was raining.
As I was walking home, it stopped raining.
While I was walking home, it was raining.
questions.explain: Wrth i = as / while.
Nes i = until. Soft mutation: d → dd.
Iddyn nhw + soft mutation: gadael → adael (g drops).
Same subject in both halves: cyn + verbnoun, with no i and no mutation.

questions.en: The children must go to bed.
questions.explain: i + noun + soft-mutated verbnoun.
Iddi hi. Ff never mutates.

units.termDef: A subordinate clause depends on a main clause and can't stand alone: 'before I miss the bus'. It is introduced by a conjunction (before, after, until). Welsh uses conjunction + i + person + verbnoun, with no tense of its own: the main clause sets the time.

units.title: Numbers and plurals
units.subtitle: tri chi, dwy gath, llawer o blant
units.rule:
Rule 1: number + SINGULAR noun. dau gi (literally 'two dog'), pum punt, deg munud. Never dau gŵn.

Rule 2: quantity word + o + PLURAL (o soft-mutates): llawer o blant, gormod o geir, digon o fwyd, ychydig o bobl. Also 'of the': dau o'r plant. Bigger numbers may use this too: tri deg chwech o gŵn.

Rule 3: 2, 3, 4 have feminine forms.

masculinefeminine
2dau + softdwy + soft
3tri + aspiratetair (no change)
4pedwarpedair

Rule 4: mutations.

  • un + feminine: soft (un gath), except ll / rh (un llaw). Masculine: none (un ci).
  • dau / dwy: soft, including ll / rh (dwy law).
  • tri / chwe: aspirate (tri chi, chwe phlentyn). Often softened or dropped in speech.
  • tair, pedwar, pedair, pum: none.
  • blynedd (years): nasal after pum, saith, wyth, naw, deng (pum mlynedd); soft after dwy (dwy flynedd); none after tair (tair blynedd).

Rule 5: short forms before a noun. pump → pum, chwech → chwe, cant → can, deg → deng (before mlynedd).

questions.explain: Number + singular noun. Tri + aspirate: c → ch.
Cath is feminine → dwy. Soft mutation, singular noun.
Merch is feminine → pedair. Pedair causes no mutation; noun stays singular.
Quantity word + o + plural. O soft-mutates: plant → blant.
Pump shortens to pum before a noun, and blynedd takes nasal mutation after it.
Blynedd is feminine → dwy, which soft-mutates: b → f.
Chwe + aspirate: p → ph. Singular noun.
Un + feminine noun: soft mutation.
Un + masculine noun: no mutation.
Dau + soft mutation: b → f. Singular noun.
Tair (feminine 3) causes no mutation.
Dwy mutates ll too: llaw → law. (Dwylo is a special word for a person's own two hands.)

questions.sentence: Mae dau blant yn yr ardd.
questions.fix: Mae dau blentyn yn yr ardd.
questions.explain: After a number the noun is singular: plentyn, not plant.

questions.sentence: Mae pedwar merch yn y dosbarth.
questions.fix: Mae pedair merch yn y dosbarth.
questions.explain: Merch is feminine, so pedair.

questions.en: There are three children in the house.
questions.answer: Mae tri phlentyn yn y tŷ
questions.explain: Tri + aspirate + singular: tri phlentyn.
'Of the' + plural: dau o'r plant.
Gormod + o + plural, soft-mutated: ceir → geir.
Blynedd is feminine → tair, which causes no mutation.

units.termDef: Cardinal numerals are counting numbers (one, two, three). Grammatical gender sorts nouns into masculine and feminine; number means singular or plural. After a numeral Welsh uses the singular noun, and some numerals change with gender (dau / dwy, tri / tair).

units.title: Comparing
units.subtitle: talach na, mwy diddorol, mor dal â, gorau
units.rule:
Three ways to compare.

Short adjectiveLong adjective
-er (than)talach namwy diddorol na
-esttalamwya diddorol
as … asmor + soft mutation + â: mor dal â, mor ddiddorol â

Than = na (nag before a vowel): talach na Tom, iau nag e. As = â (ag before a vowel). Both take the aspirate formally: na thad, â thŷ.

Spelling: b, d, g harden before -ach / -a: rhad → rhatach, gwlyb → gwlypach, teg → tecach.

Irregulars (learn these):

-er-estas … as
da (good)gwellgoraucystal â
drwg (bad)gwaethgwaethacynddrwg â
mawr (big)mwymwyacymaint â
bach (small)llailleiamor fach â
hen (old)hŷnhynamor hen â
ifanc (young)iau / ifancachieuenga / ifancamor ifanc â
hawdd (easy)hawshawsamor hawdd â

After yn the comparative soft-mutates like any adjective: Mae e'n well. Mae Caerdydd yn fwy. ll / rh don't change: yn llai, yn rhatach.

Superlative with a noun: Dyma'r caffi gorau. Tad-cu yw'r hyna. Written Welsh adds -f: gorau, hynaf, talaf.

questions.explain: Short adjective + -ach, then na. Nag only before a vowel; â means 'as'.
Long adjectives use mwy + adjective, no mutation after mwy. Mwya = most; mor = as.
Da → gwell (irregular). After yn it soft-mutates: yn well.
Mawr → mwy (irregular). After yn: yn fwy. Na Phenarth: na takes the aspirate.
Da → gwell → gorau. Superlative after y: y gorau.
Than = na before a consonant. Hŷn is the irregular comparative of hen.

questions.text: Dw i ddim mor ___ â ti.
questions.en: I'm not as tall as you.
questions.explain: Mor + soft mutation + â: mor dal â.
Ifanc → iau (ifancach is also heard). Nag before the vowel in e.

questions.en: This is the best café in Penarth.
questions.explain: Superlative follows the noun: y caffi gorau.

questions.en: The bus is cheaper than the train.
questions.answer: Mae'r bws yn rhatach na'r trên
questions.explain: Rhad → rhatach (d hardens to t). Rh doesn't mutate after yn. Na + 'r = na'r.

questions.en: The tea is as hot as the coffee.
questions.answer: Mae'r te mor boeth â'r coffi
questions.explain: Mor + soft mutation (poeth → boeth) + â. No yn before mor.

questions.sentence: Mae'r car yn mwy na'r bws.
questions.fix: Mae'r car yn fwy na'r bws.
questions.explain: Comparatives soft-mutate after yn like any adjective: yn fwy.
Fi starts with a consonant, so na, not nag.

questions.sentence: Dw i mor dal na Siôn.
questions.fix: Dw i mor dal â Siôn.
questions.explain: Mor … pairs with â (as). Na (than) goes with comparatives.
Drwg → gwaeth (irregular). After yn: yn waeth. Waetha = worst.
Hen → hŷn → hyna (written hynaf). Hŷn = older.

questions.en: This house is smaller than the other one.
questions.explain: Bach → llai (irregular). Ll doesn't mutate after yn.
Mor + soft (mawr → fawr) + â. Â takes the aspirate: tŷ → thŷ. Ag only before a vowel.
Hawdd → haws (irregular).
Superlative -a, with d → t: rhad → rhata. Rhatach = cheaper.

questions.en: She's as good as her brother.
questions.explain: As good as = cystal â (irregular). Mor dda â is heard but cystal is standard.

units.termDef: Adjectives describe nouns. Comparison has three degrees: equative (as big as: mor fawr â), comparative (bigger than: mwy na / talach na) and superlative (biggest: mwya / tala).

units.title: Bod: imperfect
units.subtitle: Ro'n i, o'n i
units.rule:
Was / were / used to. Describes a state or ongoing action in the past: Ro'n i'n byw yn Abertawe (I was living / used to live in Swansea).

StatementQuestionNegative
IRo'n iO'n i?Do'n i ddim
you (ti)Ro't tiO't ti?Do't ti ddim
he / sheRoedd e / hiOedd e / hi?Doedd e / hi ddim
weRo'n niO'n ni?Do'n ni ddim
you (chi)Ro'ch chiO'ch chi?Do'ch chi ddim
theyRo'n nhwO'n nhw?Do'n nhw ddim

Answers repeat the verb: O't ti'n hapus? → O'n / Nac o'n. Oedd e? → Oedd / Nac oedd. Never Do (that's only for the short past).

Noun subject: always singular Roedd: Roedd y plant yn chwarae. There was / wasn't: Roedd bara, Doedd dim bara.

questions.explain: Statement for I: Ro'n i. O'n i is the question form; Roedd is for he, she and nouns.
He / she / it: Roedd.
Question for they: O'n nhw? (Ro'n is the statement.)
Imperfect questions answer with the verb: Oedd / Nac oedd. Do is only for the short past (gwelais, aeth…).

questions.prompt: O't ti'n hapus yno? (Yes, I was)
questions.explain: Answer for yourself: O'n (I was).
Negative: Do'n i ddim.
They: Do'n nhw ddim.

questions.sentence: Ro'n y plant yn chwarae yn yr ardd.
questions.fix: Roedd y plant yn chwarae yn yr ardd.
questions.explain: With a noun subject the verb stays singular: Roedd, even for plural nouns.
There wasn't any X: Doedd dim X.
Question for chi: O'ch chi?
We: Ro'n ni.

questions.sentence: Ro'n e'n chwarae rygbi bob wythnos.
questions.fix: Roedd e'n chwarae rygbi bob wythnos.
questions.explain: He / she: Roedd. Ro'n is for i, ni and nhw.

options: Oedd Siân ddim yn y gwaith?
questions.explain: Question with a noun: Oedd + noun.

questions.prompt: O'ch chi'n byw yma? (No, we weren't)
questions.explain: Answering for we: (Nac) o'n.

units.termDef: The imperfect describes an ongoing state or a repeated action in the past: 'I was living', 'I used to live', 'it was raining'. Compare the simple past (preterite), which is a single completed event.

units.title: Perfect with wedi
units.subtitle: Dw i wedi bwyta
units.rule:
Have done: swap yn for wedi. Dw i'n bwyta (I'm eating) → Dw i wedi bwyta (I have eaten).

No mutation after wedi, and never wedi'n.

Questions and negatives come from bod as usual: Wyt ti wedi gorffen? → Ydw / Nac ydw. Dyn ni ddim wedi gorffen.

Had done: imperfect + wedi: Ro'n i wedi gadael (I had left).

Just done: newydd + soft mutation: Dw i newydd gyrraedd (I've just arrived).

questions.explain: Have done: wedi in place of yn.
Mae hi wedi + verbnoun, no mutation.
No mutation after wedi.
Negative perfect: Dyn ni ddim wedi…

questions.prompt: Wyt ti wedi gweld y ffilm? (Yes)
questions.explain: Wedi questions use present bod: Wyt ti…? → Ydw / Nac ydw.
Ydyn nhw + wedi + verbnoun, no mutation.
Had done: Ro'n i wedi…
Newydd = just. Unlike wedi, it takes soft mutation: c → g.
Newydd + soft mutation: g drops.
Dych chi wedi…? No mutation after wedi.

questions.sentence: Dw i ddim wedi'n gweld e.
questions.fix: Dw i ddim wedi gweld e.
questions.explain: Wedi replaces yn. Never wedi'n.
Mae … wedi = has done. Had = Roedd … wedi; just = newydd.
No mutation after wedi.
Had just: Ro'n ni newydd + soft mutation.

units.termDef: Aspect shows how an action relates to a time, rather than the time itself. The perfect links a past action to now: 'I have eaten' (Dw i wedi bwyta). The pluperfect (past perfect) puts it before another past moment: 'I had eaten' (Ro'n i wedi bwyta).

units.title: Future
units.subtitle: Bydda i
units.rule:
Will be / will be doing.

StatementQuestion / negative
IBydda iFydda i? · Fydda i ddim
you (ti)Byddi diFyddi di? · Fyddi di ddim
he / sheBydd e / hiFydd e? · Fydd e ddim
weByddwn niFyddwn ni? · Fyddwn ni ddim
you (chi)Byddwch chiFyddwch chi? · Fyddwch chi ddim
theyByddan nhwFyddan nhw? · Fyddan nhw ddim

Questions and negatives soft-mutate: B → F.

Answers: Fyddi di yno? → Bydda / Na fydda. Fydd e? → Bydd / Na fydd.

Noun subject: singular Bydd: Bydd y plant yn yr ysgol.

questions.explain: I will: Bydda i. Fydda is for questions and negatives.
questions.en: I'll be going to work tomorrow.

questions.explain: He / she / it: Bydd.
Answer for I: Bydda (no mutation in a yes).
Negative: soft mutation B → F, plus ddim.
We will: Byddwn ni.

questions.prompt: Will the children be at school?
options: Fydd y plant yn yr ysgol?
Fyddan y plant yn yr ysgol?
Bydd y plant yn yr ysgol?
Fyddan nhw'r plant yn yr ysgol?
questions.explain: Noun subject: singular Fydd, even for plural nouns. Questions soft-mutate.
Noun subject: singular Bydd.
For he: (Na) fydd.

questions.en: Will you be ready by seven?
questions.explain: Question: soft mutation B → F.
Negative: Fydda i ddim.
Byddi di = you (ti) will.

questions.sentence: Bydda i ddim yn gweithio fory.
questions.fix: Fydda i ddim yn gweithio fory.
questions.explain: Negatives soft-mutate: B → F.
Weather: Bydd hi'n…
We will: Byddwn ni.

units.termDef: The future describes what will happen. Periphrastic means it is built from an auxiliary (helping) verb, bydd-, plus yn + verbnoun, like English 'will be doing': Bydda i'n mynd.

units.title: Short-form future
units.subtitle: Gwela i, a i
units.rule:
Stem + ending, no bod: Gwela i di yfory (I'll see you tomorrow).

gwela igwelwn ni
gweli digwelwch chi
gwelith e / higwelan nhw

Irregulars:

myndgwneuddodcael
a igwna ido ica i
ei digwnei didoi dicei di
eith egwneith edaw / dith ecaiff / ceith e
awn nigwnawn nidown nicawn ni
ewch chigwnewch chidewch chicewch chi
ân nhwgwnân nhwdôn nhwcân nhw

Object soft-mutates: Prynwn ni gar.

Questions: soft mutation: Weli di? Ga i goffi? (May I have a coffee?)

Negatives: c, p, t take aspirate (Cha i ddim, Thala i ddim); everything else soft (Wela i ddim).

questions.explain: I will: stem + -a: Gwela i.
They: stem + -an.
Mynd is irregular: a i (I'll go). Es i = I went.
Gwneud: gwna i.

questions.prompt: Ga i goffi, os gwelwch yn dda?
options: May I have a coffee, please?
questions.explain: Ga i…? = May I have…? (cael, question form).
Negative: soft mutation, G drops.
Negatives of c, p, t verbs take aspirate: c → ch. (Ches i ddim = I didn't get.)
Dod: doi di; question soft-mutates D → Dd.
Dod, he: daw e (or dith e in the south).
We: -wn. The object after a short-form verb soft-mutates: car → gar. (Prynon ni = we bought.)
Questions soft-mutate the verb: G drops.
Gwneud, they: gwnân nhw. (Gwnaethon nhw = they did.)

questions.en: We'll go to Cardiff on Saturday.
questions.explain: Mynd, we: awn ni.
Negative of a t verb: aspirate t → th. (Thalais i ddim = I didn't pay.)

units.termDef: An inflected future: the verb itself takes a personal ending instead of using bod. Gwela i = I'll see. In speech it can also express a present habit.

units.title: Conditional
units.subtitle: Baswn i, hoffwn i
units.rule:
Would be / would do.

Baswn iBasen ni
Baset tiBasech chi
Basai fe / hiBasen nhw

In the south you'll also hear Byddwn i, byddet ti, byddai fe…: same meaning.

Questions and negatives soft-mutate: Faset ti'n dod? → Baswn / Na faswn. Faswn i ddim.

Handy short forms (same endings): hoffwn i (I'd like), gallwn i (I could), dylwn i (I should). They're followed by a soft-mutated word: Hoffwn i goffi. Dylech chi orffwys.

If I were: Pe bawn i'n gyfoethog, baswn i'n prynu cwch.

questions.explain: I would: Baswn i (south also Byddwn i).
Hoffwn i = I'd like.
Ti: hoffet ti. The object soft-mutates: diod → ddiod.
Negative: soft mutation B → F.
Answer for I: Baswn.
Gallwn i = I could.
Chi: dylech chi, then soft mutation (gorffwys → orffwys).
They: Basen nhw. Basai is he / she.

questions.prompt: If I were rich, I'd buy a boat.
options: Pe bawn i'n gyfoethog, baswn i'n prynu cwch.
Os dw i'n gyfoethog, baswn i'n prynu cwch.
Pe bawn i'n gyfoethog, bydda i'n prynu cwch.
Pe bawn i gyfoethog, baswn i'n prynu cwch.
Pe bawn i'n gyfoethog, prynais i gwch.
Os bawn i'n gyfoethog, baswn i'n prynu cwch.
questions.explain: Unreal 'if': pe bawn i…, then the conditional.
After dylwn i: soft mutation, m → f.
Hoffech chi = would you (chi) like.
He / she: Basai (also Base, Byddai).
Negative soft-mutates: G drops → Allwn i ddim.
Question: soft mutation, and they → Fasen nhw.

units.termDef: Mood shows the speaker's attitude to an action. The conditional expresses what would happen, often depending on a condition (an if-clause): 'I would go if…'. Modal verbs such as could, should and would like (gallwn, dylwn, hoffwn) use the same endings.

units.title: Having
units.subtitle: Mae ... gyda fi / mae gen i
units.rule:
Welsh says there's a car with me: Mae car gyda fi (I have a car).

gyda figyda ni
gyda tigyda chi
gyda fe / higyda nhw

Questions: Oes (is there): Oes car gyda ti? → Oes / Nac oes.

Negative: Does dim car gyda fi.

Past: Roedd ci gyda ni. Oedd car gyda nhw? → Oedd / Nac oedd.

North Wales: Mae gen i gar: the thing comes after gen i and soft-mutates.

questions.explain: Mae + thing + gyda + person.
Having: gyda + person.
Oes …? → Oes / Nac oes.
Does dim + thing + gyda + person.
Question: Oes + thing + gyda + person.
An indefinite thing (a car): the question is Oes.
Oes = is there / are there.
North: gen i + soft-mutated thing: ci → gi.
Past: Roedd + thing + gyda.
Mae + thing + gyda hi.
Does dim = there isn't any. Not ddim.
Past having: Roedd + thing + gyda.
Past: Oedd / Nac oedd.
gyda fe (gyda fo in the north).

units.termDef: Welsh has no verb 'to have'. It uses an existential sentence, 'there is X with me': Mae car gyda fi. Questions use oes (is there?).

units.title: Gender and plurals
units.subtitle: -au, -on, vowel change
units.rule:
Plurals have to be learnt, but the common patterns are:

add -aullyfr → llyfrau, afal → afalau
add -odcath → cathod
add -iondyn → dynion, ysgol → ysgolion
add -edmerch → merched
add -iffenest → ffenestri, gardd → gerddi
vowel changebachgen → bechgyn, car → ceir, tŷ → tai
drop -yn / -enplentyn → plant, coeden → coed, blodyn → blodau
irregularci → cŵn, llaw → dwylo (pair), athro → athrawon

Gender: feminine singular nouns soft-mutate after y and mutate their adjective: y gath fach. Masculine: y ci bach. Plurals never mutate after y: y cathod, y merched.

questions.explain: llyfr + -au.
cath → cathod, and llawer o + soft mutation → gathod.
Singulars in -yn drop it in the plural: plentyn → plant.
tŷ → tai (vowel change).
Plurals never soft-mutate after y, even feminine ones.
Plural: no mutation of the noun or the adjective.
Vowel change: bachgen → bechgyn.
ffenest + -ri.

questions.sentence: Mae'r gath fawr a'r ci fach yn chwarae.
questions.fix: Mae'r gath fawr a'r ci bach yn chwarae.
questions.explain: Ci is masculine: the adjective doesn't mutate.
athro → athrawon.
Numbers take the singular: dau + soft mutation → dau gar.
ci → cŵn (irregular).
Plurals don't mutate after y / 'r.
llaw → dwylo (literally 'two hands').

units.termDef: Every Welsh noun is masculine or feminine (grammatical gender), which affects mutation after y and on adjectives. Plurals are formed by adding an ending (a suffix), by vowel change (internal change), or by removing a singular ending.

units.title: This and that
units.subtitle: hwn, hon, hyn, 'ma, 'na
units.rule:
After a noun (with y / yr / 'r in front):

this / thesethat / those
masculiney llyfr hwny llyfr hwnnw
femininey gath hony gath honno
pluraly plant hyny plant hynny
speech, anyy llyfr 'may llyfr 'na

Feminine nouns still soft-mutate after y: y gath hon.

On their own (pronouns): hwn / hon (this one), hwnna / honna (that one), hyn (this, these: ideas), hynny (that, those: ideas). Beth ydy hwnna? ar hyn o bryd (at the moment).

Dyma (here is / this is) and dyna (there is / that is) + soft mutation: Dyma gar newydd. Dyna'r broblem.

Time: y bore 'ma (this morning), y prynhawn 'ma, heno (tonight), eleni (this year).

questions.explain: Llyfr is masculine: hwn. Keep y in front.
Cath is feminine: hon, and soft mutation after y.
Plural: hyn (in speech, 'ma).
In speech: 'na for 'that' with any noun (carefully: hwnnw).
Plural 'those': hynny (in speech, y tai 'na).
This morning: y bore 'ma.
That (thing): hwnna. Hwn = this.
Dyma + soft mutation: c → g.
Dyna = that is / there is. Problem is feminine: y broblem.
Cath is feminine: hon, not hwn.
Hyn = this (as an idea): ar hyn o bryd.

questions.text: Dw i ddim yn gwybod dim am ___.
questions.en: I don't know anything about that.
questions.explain: An idea or situation: hynny (in speech also hwnna).
Plural, spoken: 'ma (carefully: yr esgidiau hyn).

questions.prompt: Which one do you want, this one or that one? (masculine)
options: Pa un dych chi eisiau, hwn neu hwnna?
Pa un dych chi eisiau, hon neu honna?
Pa un dych chi eisiau, hyn neu hynny?
Pa un dych chi eisiau, 'ma neu 'na?
Pa un dych chi'n eisiau, hwn neu hwnna?
Pwy un dych chi eisiau, hwn neu hwnna?
questions.explain: Masculine pronouns: hwn (this one), hwnna (that one). 'Ma and 'na only follow a noun.

units.termDef: Demonstratives point to something by nearness. As determiners they go with a noun (this book: y llyfr hwn); as pronouns they stand alone (this one: hwn). This / these are near; that / those are further away or already mentioned.

units.title: Nasal mutation: yn (in)
units.subtitle: yng Nghaerdydd
units.rule:
yn = in causes nasal mutation, and changes its own shape to match:

c → nghyng Nghaerdydd
g → ngyng Ngwynedd
p → mhym Mhen-y-bont
b → mym Mangor
t → nhyn Nhregaron
d → nyn Ninbych

Other letters don't change: yn Llundain, yn Aberystwyth.

yn is for definite places (names, y / 'r): yn y tŷ. For a / any: mewn tŷ (in a house).

questions.explain: c → ngh, and yn → yng.
b → m.
t → nh.
p → mh, and yn → ym.
Only c, p, t, g, b, d change. Ll stays.

questions.answer: Mae fy chwaer yn byw yng Ngwynedd
questions.explain: g → ng, and yn → yng.
d → n after yn (in).
In a (indefinite): mewn, no mutation. Yn y tŷ = in the house.
c → ngh.
Vowels don't change.
c → ngh after yn (in).
b → m.
t → nh, and yn stays yn.

questions.en: We were on holiday in Barmouth (Bermo).
questions.answer: Ro'n ni ar wyliau ym Mermo
questions.explain: b → m, and yn → ym.

units.termDef: Nasal mutation changes p→mh, t→nh, c→ngh, b→m, d→n, g→ng. Its main triggers are fy (my) and yn meaning 'in'.

units.title: Aspirate mutation
units.subtitle: a, â, gyda, tri, chwe
units.rule:
Only c, p, t change: c → ch, p → ph, t → th.

a (and)bara a chaws
â, gyda (with)gyda Thom
tri (3, masculine)tri phlentyn
chwe (6)chwe chath
ei (her)ei thad hi
tua (about)tua thri o'r gloch
na (than / nor)yn dalach na Thom

Before a vowel a → ac, â → ag, gyda → gydag: afal ac oren.

Tair (3, feminine) causes no mutation: tair cath.

questions.explain: a (and) + aspirate: c → ch.
a + aspirate: c → ch. (ac only before a vowel.)
tri + singular + aspirate: p → ph.
chwe before a noun (chwech on its own) + aspirate.
gyda + aspirate: T → Th.
ei (her) + aspirate. ei dad e = his father.
tua + aspirate: t → th.

questions.en: I went with Catrin and Pedr.
questions.answer: Es i gyda Chatrin a Phedr
questions.explain: gyda and a both aspirate: C → Ch, P → Ph.

questions.sentence: Dw i'n hoffi te a coffi.
questions.fix: Dw i'n hoffi te a choffi.
questions.explain: a (and) + aspirate: c → ch.
na (than) + aspirate.
Car is masculine: tri + singular + aspirate.

questions.sentence: Mae tri cath yn yr ardd.
questions.fix: Mae tair cath yn yr ardd.
questions.explain: Cath is feminine: tair, which causes no mutation.
Before a vowel, a → ac.
gyda + aspirate: P → Ph. (gydag only before a vowel.)

units.termDef: Aspirate mutation only affects c→ch, p→ph, t→th. Its triggers include a (and), â / gyda (with), tri, chwe, ei (her), tua and na.

units.title: Inflected prepositions
units.subtitle: arna i, ata i, amdana i
units.rule:
Some prepositions take a personal ending before a pronoun.

ar (on)at (to, towards)am (about, for)
iarna iata iamdana i
tiarnat tiatat tiamdanat ti
fearno feato feamdano fe
hiarni hiati hiamdani hi
niarnon niaton niamdanon ni
chiarnoch chiatoch chiamdanoch chi
nhwarnyn nhwatyn nhwamdanyn nhw

Feelings sit 'on' you: Mae annwyd arna i (I've a cold), ofn (afraid), syched (thirsty), eisiau bwyd (hungry), hiraeth (longing). Questions: Oes ofn arni hi?

Verbs that need them: edrych ar, gwrando ar, aros am, meddwl am, poeni am, ysgrifennu at, anfon at.

questions.explain: ar + i → arna i.
meddwl am; am + ti → amdanat ti.
ar + fe → arno fe.
Feelings: Oes + feeling + ar + person.
ysgrifennu at; at + nhw → atyn nhw.
ar + me → arna i.
ar + ni → arnon ni.
am + fe → amdano fe.
at + hi → ati hi.
Hungry = eisiau bwyd ar + person.
Match the person: arno fe (him), arnyn nhw (them).
aros am; am + i → amdana i.
poeni am; am + nhw → amdanyn nhw.
ar + ti → arnat ti.

units.termDef: A preposition shows a relationship of place, direction or topic: on, to, about. Inflected (conjugated) prepositions take a personal ending before a pronoun: ar + i → arna i.

units.title: 'That' clauses
units.subtitle: bod, fy mod i
units.rule:
After saying, thinking, knowing etc., mae / roedd becomes bod: Dw i'n credu bod hi'n bwrw glaw. It covers is, are, was and were. Dwedodd e bod y bws yn hwyr.

With pronouns (careful style; colloquially bod fi, bod ti…):

fy mod iein bod ni
dy fod tieich bod chi
ei fod eeu bod nhw
ei bod hi

The mutations are the usual possessive ones: fy nasal (mod), dy / ei (his) soft (fod), ei (her) none (bod).

Had / has done: bod … wedi: Clywais i eich bod chi wedi gadael.

options: Dw i'n credu bod hi'n bwrw glaw.
Dw i'n credu mae hi'n bwrw glaw.
Dw i'n credu bod hi bwrw glaw.
Dw i'n credu ydy hi'n bwrw glaw.
Dw i'n credu bod hi'n bwrw'n glaw.
Dw i'n credu yn bod hi'n bwrw glaw.
questions.explain: After credu: bod replaces mae.

questions.text: Mae Siân yn dweud ___ hi'n brysur.
questions.explain: that (is) = bod.

questions.prompt: I know that he's at home.
options: Dw i'n gwybod ei fod e gartre.
Dw i'n gwybod ei bod e gartre.
Dw i'n gwybod ei fod hi gartre.
Dw i'n gwybod mae e gartre.
Dw i'n gwybod ei mod e gartre.
Dw i'n gwybod fy mod e gartre.
questions.explain: He: ei fod e (soft mutation after ei = his).

questions.text: Dw i'n siŵr ei ___ hi'n iawn.
questions.explain: ei (her): b doesn't change → ei bod hi.
fy + nasal mutation: b → m.

questions.en: He said that they were tired.
questions.answer: Dwedodd e eu bod nhw wedi blino
questions.explain: They: eu bod nhw. Bod also covers 'were'.
alts: Dwedodd e bod nhw wedi blino

questions.prompt: I heard that you (chi) had left.
options: Clywais i eich bod chi wedi gadael.
Clywais i eich fod chi wedi gadael.
Clywais i eich bod chi'n wedi gadael.
Clywais i roeddech chi wedi gadael.
Clywais i eu bod chi wedi gadael.
Clywais i ein bod chi wedi gadael.
questions.explain: You (chi): eich bod chi; had left: wedi gadael.

questions.sentence: Dw i'n meddwl mae'r siop ar gau.
questions.fix: Dw i'n meddwl bod y siop ar gau.
questions.explain: After meddwl / credu / gwybod, mae becomes bod.

options: Dw i'n falch dy fod ti yma.
Dw i'n falch dy bod ti yma.
Dw i'n falch ti fod yma.
Dw i'n falch wyt ti yma.
Dw i'n falch dy fod ti'n yma.
Dw i'n falch dy mod ti yma.
questions.explain: dy + soft mutation: dy fod ti. No 'n before yma.
They: eu bod nhw.

questions.prompt: I didn't know that the shop had closed.
options: Do'n i ddim yn gwybod bod y siop wedi cau.
Do'n i ddim yn gwybod bod y siop wedi gau.
Do'n i ddim yn gwybod roedd y siop wedi cau.
Do'n i ddim yn gwybod bod y siop yn wedi cau.
Do'n i ddim yn gwybod mae'r siop wedi cau.
Do'n i ddim yn gwybod bod siop wedi cau.
questions.explain: Had closed: bod … wedi cau (no mutation after wedi).

questions.sentence: Mae e'n dweud ei bod e'n sâl.
questions.fix: Mae e'n dweud ei fod e'n sâl.
questions.explain: He: ei fod e. Ei bod is for hi.

questions.answer: Dw i'n credu ein bod ni'n hwyr
questions.explain: We: ein bod ni.
alts: Dw i'n credu bod ni'n hwyr

questions.explain: Colloquially bod ti; carefully dy fod ti.

units.termDef: A noun clause works as the object of a verb such as say, think or know: 'I think [that it's raining]'. Reporting what someone said this way is indirect (reported) speech. In Welsh, bod replaces mae / roedd in the clause.

units.title: Negatives with mo
units.subtitle: Welais i mo'r ffilm
units.rule:
With a short-form verb (past or future) and a definite object (the…, a name, a pronoun), ddim becomes mo:

Welais i mo'r ffilm (I didn't see the film). Welon ni mo Siân.

mohono imohonon ni
mohonot timohonoch chi
mohono fe / mohoni himohonyn nhw

Indefinite object (a / any / none): keep ddim, no mutation: Brynais i ddim car.

Bod sentences never use mo: Dw i ddim yn nabod y dyn.

questions.explain: Definite object after a short-form verb: mo'r (= ddim + o'r).
Definite: mo'r.
Pronoun: mo + ending: mohono fe.
Indefinite object (a car): ddim, no mutation of car.
Definite: mo'r.
Definite object: mo'r, not ddim y.
Her: mohoni hi.
A name is definite: mo, and no 'r.
Definite plural: still mo'r. (Ff never mutates.)
Them: mohonyn nhw.
Indefinite (any bread): ddim, not mo.
You (chi): mohonoch chi.

options: Dw i ddim yn nabod y dyn.
Dw i mo'n nabod y dyn.
Dw i ddim yn nabod mo'r dyn.
Dw i mo nabod y dyn.
Dw i mo'r yn nabod dyn.
Dw i ddim nabod y dyn.
questions.explain: Mo is only for short-form verbs. With bod + yn, just ddim.
Definite: mo'r te.

units.termDef: Negative sentences with an inflected verb and a definite object (the…, a name or a pronoun) use mo instead of ddim. Definite means a specific known thing; indefinite means 'a' or 'any'.

units.title: Commands
units.subtitle: Ewch, cer, paid
units.rule:
Chi (polite or plural): stem + -wch: Eisteddwch, Edrychwch, Gwrandewch, Arhoswch, Rhowch.

Ti (friend, child): stem + -a: Eistedda, Edrycha, Gwranda, Arhosa.

chiti (south)
goEwchCer
comeDewchDere
doGwnewchGwna
giveRhowchRho

Don't: Peidiwch â (chi) / Paid â (ti) + verbnoun with aspirate: Peidiwch â phoeni. Paid â chyffwrdd. Before a vowel â → ag: Peidiwch ag anghofio.

questions.explain: Dod, chi: Dewch.
Mynd, ti: Cer (Dos in the north). Ewch is chi.
Stem + -wch.
Peidiwch â + aspirate: p → ph. Paid is for ti.
â + aspirate: c → ch.
Chi: -wch; please: os gwelwch yn dda.
Dod, ti: Dere (Tyrd in the north).
â + aspirate: t → th.
Rhoi, ti: Rho (chi: Rhowch).
Gwrando, chi: Gwrandewch. Gwranda is ti.
Before a vowel, â → ag.
Gwneud, ti: Gwna. Gwnewch is chi.
Paid â + bod (b doesn't aspirate).
Someone you'd call chi: -wch.

units.termDef: The imperative mood gives commands, instructions and requests: 'Sit down', 'Don't worry'. Welsh has a familiar singular form (ti) and a polite or plural form (chi). A negative imperative uses paid / peidiwch â.

units.title: Emphatic sentences
units.subtitle: Fi sy'n...
units.rule:
Put the important word first.

Subject first → sy: Fi sy'n gyrru (It's me who's driving). Pwy sy'n dod? Never Pwy mae.

Past: subject + short-form verb (3rd person): Tom enillodd (It was Tom who won). Pwy wnaeth e? (Who did it?)

Identity: Athro ydy e (He's a teacher). Meddyg dw i. Cymraes ydy hi.

Anything else first keeps the normal verb: Yn y gegin mae hi. Coffi dw i eisiau.

Negative: Nid fi sy ar fai (colloquially Dim fi…).

questions.explain: Fronted subject + sy.
Pwy as subject: Pwy sy'n…
Identity: noun first, then ydy (also yw).
Noun first: Meddyg dw i.
Past emphatic: subject + 3rd-person past verb.

units.termDef: A cleft sentence splits a statement to highlight one part: 'It's me who is driving'. Welsh does this by fronting: moving the emphasised element to the start of the sentence.

units.title: Relative clauses
units.subtitle: sy, a
units.rule:
Who / which is: sy: y dyn sy'n byw drws nesa. y siop sy ar gau.

Was / will be: oedd, fydd: y fenyw oedd yn canu, y bobl fydd yn dod.

Short-form verbs: a + soft mutation: y llyfr a brynais i (the book I bought), y dyn a ffoniodd. In speech a is often dropped but the mutation stays: y ffilm welais i.

Never pwy in these: pwy is only for questions.

Negative: y plant sy ddim yn dod.

options: y plant sy ddim yn dod

a + soft mutation: c → g.
a + soft mutation, but ff never mutates.
a + soft mutation: p → b.

units.termDef: A relative clause describes a noun, like an adjective: 'the man [who lives next door]'. English uses relative pronouns (who, which, that). Welsh uses sy, a + soft mutation, oedd or fydd.

glossary.def: When an action happens: present, past, future.
How an action relates to a time: ongoing, completed, or connected to now (perfect).
The speaker's attitude: indicative (facts), imperative (commands), conditional (would).
Now or generally true: Dw i'n mynd (I'm going / I go).
A completed past event: Es i (I went).
An ongoing or habitual past state: Ro'n i'n mynd (I was going / used to go).
A past action linked to now: Dw i wedi mynd (I have gone).
Before another past moment: Ro'n i wedi mynd (I had gone).
Will happen: Bydda i'n mynd, A i (I'll go).
Would happen: Baswn i'n mynd (I would go).
A command: Ewch! Cer! (Go!)
A helping verb used to build a tense: bod, bydd-, gwneud.
Built with an auxiliary verb plus a verbnoun: Bydda i'n gweld.
The verb takes a personal ending: gwelais i, gwela i.
The basic form of a verb (to go / going): mynd, bwyta. Welsh's 'infinitive'.
The part of a verb that endings attach to: gwel- in gweld, pryn- in prynu.
Subject: who does the action. Object: what it is done to. In 'Siân bought a car', Siân is the subject, a car the object.
Definite: a specific known thing (the car, Siân, it). Indefinite: a / any (a car).
Noun: a thing, person or place. Adjective: describes a noun (big, small).
Every noun is masculine or feminine; it affects mutations and some numbers.
A word before a noun that specifies it: the, this, my.
Shows ownership: my, your, his, her (fy, dy, ei).
Points to something: this, that, these, those (hwn, hon, hyn, 'na).
Shows a relationship: on, to, with, about (ar, at, gyda, am).
A preposition with a personal ending: arna i, ati hi.
Stands in for a noun: I, you, he, she, it (fi, ti, fe, hi).
A group of words with its own verb. Main clause: stands alone. Subordinate clause: depends on another.
Joins words or clauses: and, before, after, until (a, cyn, ar ôl, nes).
Describes a noun: the man who lives here (y dyn sy'n byw yma).
A clause that is the object of say / think / know: I think that… (bod).
Highlights one part by moving it to the front: Fi sy'n gyrru.
Making a sentence negative: ddim, dim, mo.
A change to the first consonant of a word caused by the word before it.
as big as / bigger / biggest: mor fawr â, mwy, mwya.
